label: checker-a
statement: Reviewed all 40 current typed tools across all eight batches using only classifier-contract.md and the final checker-a-sample.json; no quarantine file was read. All 14 sampled optional analogs use actual listed roles and useful concrete correspondences. This bounded sample does not claim exhaustive analog review.

judgments.reason: Seek, avoidance and separation weights change combined acceleration and the selected units' trajectories.
Separation, cohesion and velocity-match weights alter flock spacing, centroid movement and heading variance.
Steering ranks and an acceleration threshold select the active significant steering group, changing movement and switches.
Seek precedes wander; the acceleration threshold makes fallback activate near equilibrium and changes stalled steps.
Slot spacing changes fixed slot positions and formation width for the selected squad, with measurable slot error.
Travel, danger and visibility costs reweight selected regions and can change the chosen route and route cost.
Source strength and radius change the influence field around selected units and the resulting control frontier.
A distance-decay exponent changes influence falloff, while source strength changes its magnitude and reach.
The influence radius changes the field boundary and the number of terrain regions affected by selected sources.
A terrain cost multiplier reweights edges through selected regions and can divert unit routes.
Anchor speed moves the formation reference while slot spacing sets subordinate positions, changing trajectories and formation error.
Distance, danger and exposure weights change edge costs and the routes selected from those costs.
A numeric selector threshold admits or drops whole unit messages, visibly changing delivery counts.
Recipient count controls copies routed to a numbered receiving set, changing deliveries and copy count.
The next sequence number gates release from a bounded reorder buffer, making consecutive delivery observable.
The send window caps unacknowledged progress, changing outstanding messages and sender blocking time.
Pool size and per-performer capacity route received work to available performers, changing listener blocking and backlog.
The type count defines numbered type-specific routes; message type determines its receiving channel and mismatch count.

Subscriber count and notification delay change which units receive notifications and when delivery occurs.
One completion-gated active input serializes queued messages. Executor and planner correspondence is sequencing dependent mutations after prior closure.

Squad size forms visible membership of 7–9 units. Operator and planner correspondence is an explicit worker cap with measured coordination cost.
Messages per tick changes channel admission and backlog. Operator and planner correspondence is limiting repeated requests and status traffic.
